hook_text: A turtle swims thousands of kilometres just to lay her eggs on one beach in KwaZulu-Natal. Why that beach?
clip_script: iSimangaliso, KwaZulu-Natal. A habitat is not just a place. It is a supermarket, a tap, a bedroom, a nursery and a hiding place. Hippos graze the grass and cool off in the lake. A reedbuck freezes in the reeds. A crab dives into its hole. And on a summer night, a loggerhead turtle crawls up the beach, digs a hole and lays about a hundred eggs. Food, water, shelter, babies, escape. Take away the habitat, and you take away all five.
visual_style: Whiteboard wetland with five icons appearing over it: food, water, shelter, babies and escape, each linked to an animal.
mood: Warm and caring, like a nature programme.
pacing: Five needs, one quick animal story for each, then what happens when a habitat is damaged.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and list what a bird in your school grounds needs from its habitat.
